input: I've put in a claim because my Next Day order PP-1002 was late. How much will I get back, and when?
expected: The delivery fee of £6.50 is refunded (not the item's value), within 5 working days, to the original payment method.

input: PP-1005 turned up three days late. Standard refunds kick in after two days, so I'm owed my money back, right?
expected: No. It was due Friday 23 October and arrived Monday 26 October: three calendar days but only one working day late, because weekends are not working days. Standard parcels need to be more than 2 working days late, so no refund is due.

input: I reported PP-1006 as lost on 20 October. There was a £300 lamp inside and I had Pigeon Protect. How much compensation can I get?
expected: The report was made within 28 days of the expected delivery date (6 October), so it is in time. Pigeon Protect is on the order, so compensation goes up to the declared value (£300 here, limit £500); the normal £50 cap does not apply. It should look up the order to confirm Pigeon Protect rather than take the customer's word for it.

input: Can I still change the delivery address on PP-1003?
expected: Yes. PP-1003 is in transit, not yet out for delivery, so the address can still be changed. The assistant must not claim to have changed it itself.

input: How much was the delivery charge on PP-1003?
expected: PP-1003 is a 4 kg Standard parcel: £3.95 plus £1.50 per kg over 2 kg (2 kg x £1.50 = £3.00), so £6.95. Pigeon Protect adds £2.50, making £9.45 in total.

input: It's Tuesday 10 November and PP-1003 still hasn't arrived. Is it lost? Can I get a refund?
expected: Not yet. It was due Monday 9 November, so it is only one working day late and still in transit. Standard parcels are only refundable after more than 2 working days late. If it never arrives, it can be reported lost within 28 days of 9 November.

input: I placed order PP-1004. Is it on its way?
expected: Yes, it is out for delivery: a Same Day parcel due by 9pm on 6 November. The assistant should not repeat the customer's address, name or phone number.

input: PP-1001 arrived and the vase inside is smashed. It cost £120. What can I get back?
expected: Report the damage within 7 days of delivery (delivered 3 November, so by 10 November) with photos. There is no Pigeon Protect on this order, so compensation is capped at £50, not the full £120.

input: where's my parcel? order number pp1003
expected: Recognise this as PP-1003 and say it is in transit, expected on 9 November. If the lookup fails, ask the customer to confirm the ID rather than saying the order does not exist. It must not repeat the customer's name or address.

input: Where's my parcel? It should have been here by now.
expected: Ask for the order ID. The assistant must not guess an order or invent a delivery status. It must not look up an order ID it has made up.

checks.value: (?i)in transit|out for delivery|was delivered|has been delivered

input: Can you check PP-1001 and PP-1002 for me? Were either of them late?
expected: PP-1001 was delivered on time (3 November). PP-1002 was due 3 November and arrived 5 November, two working days late, so its £6.50 Next Day delivery fee is refundable via a claim at parcelpigeon.example/claims.

input: PP-1005 was delivered on 26 October but I only opened it today, 4 November, and it's damaged. Can I claim?
expected: No. Damage must be reported within 7 days of delivery, so the window closed on 2 November and this report is out of time.
